### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A27, A28 and A29 each took part in about half of the traces (52, 48 and 48 in 100) and never repeated within a trace; in the later window, each of the three takes part in every trace, exactly once [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003].
- Earlier, the three were mutually exclusive: every trace contained either A27 alone (about 52 in 100) or A28 together with A29 (about 48 in 100), and A27 never co-occurred with A28 or A29 (0 of 200 traces). In the later window, all three run in every trace, with A28 and A29 in either order (about 50/50) and both always before A27 [REL013, REL014, REL015].
- Routing changed at the borders of this group: A20's only observed successor was earlier A21, in the later window it is A28 or A29 (about 50/50); A23's observed outgoing transitions, earlier split between A27 (about 52 in 100), A29 (about 27) and A28 (about 21), now always go to A27; A28 and A29, which earlier led mostly to A24, now lead to each other or to A21 [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004].
- The order between the A28/A29 pair and A21/A23 flipped: earlier, A21 and A23 preceded A28 and A29 in every trace containing both; in the later window, A28 and A29 precede A21 and A23 in every trace. A20, A21 and A23 still precede A27, and A27, A28 and A29 all still precede A24 [REL005, REL006, REL008, REL009, REL001, REL004, REL007, REL010, REL011, REL012].
- Event distances shifted accordingly: A21 is now 3 positions after A20 (was 1) and A23 is 5 after A20 (was 3), while A28 and A29 moved from 4–5 positions after A20 to 1–2; A21→A24 is now consistently 4 positions (was 4–5) and A23→A24 consistently 2 (was 2–3), and A24 follows A28, respectively A29, at 5 positions in about half of the later traces each (99 and 101 of 200) [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008].
- Relative event positions moved in the same direction: A28 and A29 sit earlier (mean about 0.53 to about 0.44), while A21, A23, A27 and A24 sit slightly later (for example A21 from about 0.43 to about 0.49) [POS005, POS006, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004].

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the earlier exclusive choice between "A27 only" and "A28 with A29" was replaced by a flow in which A28 and A29 (in either order) always execute directly after A20, ahead of A21 and A23, with A27 then running before A24 — so all three activities now occur in every case instead of in roughly half. The relational evidence is direct: the order between A28/A29 and A21/A23 flipped from "A21 and A23 first" in every earlier trace to "A28 and A29 first" in every later trace, the previously unobserved co-occurrences of A27 with A28 and with A29 rose from 0 to 200 of 200 traces, and the successor profiles of A20 and A23 changed completely, which shows a placement and participation change directly rather than a mere frequency shift [REL005, REL006, REL008, REL009, REL013, REL014, DIR001, DIR002].

The 36 qualifying items are many times the roughly 0.44 items expected by chance when screening 89 units, so chance alone cannot account for the evidence as a whole; each item's difference is also larger than in about 199 of 200 random re-splits, and the occurrence, routing, relation, position and lag items all fit one coherent reconstruction, with proportions resting on 96–200 observations per window [OCC001, REL015, LAG001, LAG002, POS005, POS006].

Limitations: this describes behaviour across two finite windows, not a verified model modification. A shift in the mix of pre-existing variants between the windows is the main competing explanation; the completeness of the changes (0 to 200 of 200 traces, order flips in every trace) makes pure sampling fluctuation implausible, but the evidence cannot show whether sequence parts not covered by the tested pairs (for example between A21 and A23) also changed, and items sharing the same traces are not independent confirmations [REL015, LAG007, LAG008].
